commonErrors.why: You divided the fines directly by liters. molarity moles per liter, It is necessary to divide by the molar mass first; Your output unit is g/L not mol/L.
You stopped at the number of moles and did not divide by the volume.. 0.100 is n, not M.
You multiplied by the volume instead of dividing by it.

questions.solution: ‎C₂ = C₁V₁ / V₂ = (2.00 × 25.0) / 100.0 = 0.500 mol/L‎. The volume has become four times its volume and the concentration has become a quarter.

commonErrors.why: You inverted the ratio and calculated C₁V₂/V₁. Dilution always decreases concentration. Any result greater than 2.00 is an error without needing to review the calculation.
You wrote the original concentration. Adding water does not leave the concentration the same; The constant is the number of moles, not the concentration.
You omitted a conversion or over-divided 1000. The units mL at both ends are deleted, and there is no need to convert at all.
You multiplied by 250 without converting to litres. One hundred moles in a small cup is an unreasonable value, and this is a sufficient mark to review the unit.
You divided the concentration on volume. Moles are a product, not a division, : n = C × V.
You divide the volume by the concentration.
You divided by the mass of the solvent 180.0 g, not by the mass of the solution 200.0 g. The solution is both solute and solvent, and this is the most common error of this pattern.
You write the mass of the solute in grams rather than percentages.
You divided by 220, meaning you counted the solute twice in the denominator.

questions.solution: ‎V₁ = C₂V₂ / C₁ = (0.300 × 500.0) / 6.00 = 150 / 6.00 = 25.0 mL‎. The volume is then supplemented with water to 500.0 mL.

commonErrors.why: You inverted the ratio and calculated C₁V₂/C₂. A concentrated solution always requires a volume smaller than the final volume. An output greater than 500 is a clear error.
You calculated the volume of water added, not the volume of the concentrated solution. The required V₁, and the water added is 500 − 25 = 475 mL.
You stopped at the product C₂V₂ = 150 and did not divide it by C₁.
